riskAssessment.reviewNotes: The API is standalone and path-loaded by focused tests so shared module registration, architecture tests, and coverage policy remain untouched.

acceptance: The standalone boundary accepts explicit Important Structural Change, Top5 Change, Stage Transition, Rising, and Dropped facts and preserves every supplied event identity, period, company, opaque fact value, and per-section insertion order.

WeeklyChangeCompression exposes explicit sections in deterministic order: Important Structural Change, Top5 Change, Stage Transition, Rising, Dropped, and No Change; no section is inferred from Stage, Ranking, Distance, score, or raw evidence.
The compression rejects blank boundary values, period mismatches, and duplicate event identities deterministically without mutating accepted input collections.
When no change events are supplied, No Change is emitted with the stable label NO_CHANGE, the supplied period, and zero counts for all five change sections; it emits no narrative text.

When change events are supplied, the same stable No Change section boundary remains inspectable without fabricating a No Change event; all non-empty event sections retain their exact input facts and order.

The standalone source imports only Rust standard-library facilities, contains no crate or cross-feature imports, is not registered through src/features/weekly_radar/domain/mod.rs, and contains no Threshold Distance, Stage inference, Ranking, score, persistence, renderer, scheduler, delivery, or runtime/provider implementation.

Focused module-local and integration tests exercise all five event sections, specified section ordering, fact/order retention, stable No Change, duplicate/period guards, and source-level non-inference boundaries.

The design spec, implementation plan, reference-impact evidence, Summary, Outcome, and strict AI Cockpit lifecycle records capture the authorization, scope, verification evidence, limitations, and local-only next action.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Keep the compression boundary standalone and independent of shared Weekly Radar module registration and other feature implementations.
Consume only explicit upstream facts; do not infer or recalculate Stage, Ranking, Distance, score, Top5 membership, Rising, or Dropped.
Preserve supplied event identity, field values, and insertion order exactly; do not manufacture narrative text.
Reject duplicate event identities and period conflicts deterministically without silently merging or overwriting input.
Resolve problems discovered within this Work Item in the current Work Item and record the fix in Summary, checkpoints, and Outcome; do not open a new WI for an in-scope correction.
Do not introduce rendering, persistence, delivery, scheduler, retry, trading, price prediction, target price, portfolio allocation, or capital-action behavior.

intent.problem: WR-002 through WR-006 provide explicit Weekly Radar facts, but there is no deterministic boundary that compresses the five important weekly-change sections into a stable downstream shape while retaining the supplied facts and order.
constraints: Only write the declared WR-007 source, focused module-local/integration tests, design/plan, reference-impact, and governed evidence paths; do not edit shared mod.rs, architecture tests, or the shared coverage policy.

Important Structural Change, Top5 Change, Stage Transition, Rising, and Dropped inputs are already explicit upstream facts. Preserve them without recomputing Stage, Ranking, Distance, score, membership, or event meaning.
No Change must have a stable deterministic output with a fixed label and explicit zero counts when the input has no events; no narrative text may be generated.

The user authorized execution, verification, publication, merge, close, and archive for all 24 planned Work Items, while this local WI execution is explicitly limited to no push, no PR, no merge, and no close.
intent.rationale: A standalone section-preserving aggregate gives later renderers a deterministic compression boundary without allowing compression to reinterpret domain facts or depend on shared module wiring owned by another Work Item.
